title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator for fly walking.
source_locator: Abstract; Fig. 5d,e; Supplementary Video 2 legend (publisher web preview)
quote: Simulations also predicted that a separate descending pathway (DNb08) drives rhythmic leg movements, which we confirmed experimentally using optogenetics in behaving flies.
mapping_basis: Paper uses the MANC/Namiki type name DNb08 directly.
effector: unspecified optogenetic effector (not stated in accessible text)
notes: Abstract says 'behaving flies'; the Fig. 5 title ('DNb08 produces rhythmic leg movements in simulations and headless flies') and the Supplementary Video 2 legend ('Optogenetic activation of DNb08 neurons drives oscillatory leg movements in headless flies.') from the publisher web preview show the preparation was headless. Rhythmic leg movement was confirmed, but which legs is not stated in accessible text, so each pair is coded 'unclear'. Driver line, effector and headless surface unknown (Methods paywalled).

title: A neural command circuit for grooming movement control.
source_locator: Fig. 2A,B; Results 'Three different interneuron classes elicit antennal grooming'
quote: For example, aDN1-spGAL4-1 flies spent 4.8% of their time grooming their antennae vs 66.1% for aBN2-spGAL4-2 (Figure 2B, black boxes).
mapping_basis: synonyms.csv maps aDN1 (literature, Hampel 2015) to DNg62 only; driver_lines.csv lists aDN1-spGAL4-1 as DNg62.
penetrance: small but increased antennal grooming (4.8% of time)
notes: Antennal grooming scored manually from video. Front legs coded yes because the Discussion states that the circuit elicits 'the front leg movements that constitute antennal grooming'. Other legs not described. Fig. 2I shows expression only in aDN1. Antennal amputation did not significantly change grooming for this line (Fig. 2B, n.s.).

title: A neural command circuit for grooming movement control.
quote: Two other spGAL4 pairs also targeted aBN1 and were able to elicit antennal grooming with thermogenetic activation (aBN1-spGAL4-2, aBN1/aDN1-spGAL4, Figure 2I, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C).
mapping_basis: synonyms.csv maps aDN1 to DNg62 only; driver_lines.csv lists aBN1/DN1-spGAL4 as DNg62 with aBN1 off-target.
other_cell_types: additional non-DN cells marked in Fig. 2I
notes: The line labels aBN1 as well as aDN1, and aBN1 alone elicits antennal grooming, so the effect cannot be attributed to aDN1. Grooming increased after antennal amputation (Fig. 2B). Front legs inferred from the Discussion (antennal grooming = front leg movements).

title: A neural command circuit for grooming movement control.
quote: induced antennal grooming with thermogenetic activation using dTrpA1 were identified by screening over 1500 randomly selected GAL4 lines (R39A11, R26B12, and R18C11-GAL4)
mapping_basis: R18C11-GAL4 (aDN-GAL4) labels three aDNs; aDN1 is one of them (aDN1-spGAL4-1 uses the R18C11 enhancer, Fig. 2G); aDN1 maps to DNg62 in synonyms.csv.
other_cell_types: other neuronal populations in the GAL4 pattern (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C)
n_flies_note: n = 10 per line (Fig. 2—fig. suppl. 1A); n >= 10 (Fig. 1—fig. suppl. 1A)
notes: R18C11-GAL4 (= aDN-GAL4) is a broad GAL4 line. Fig. 1—fig. suppl. 1A shows significantly increased antennal grooming (median about 20% of time). Front legs inferred from the Discussion.

title: A neural command circuit for grooming movement control.
quote: Both of these lines elicit antennal grooming with thermogenetic activation, and aDN-LexA targets three aDN neurons
mapping_basis: aDN-LexA (R18C11 enhancer) targets three aDNs, including aDN1 (Fig. 4—fig. suppl. 2E); aDN1 maps to DNg62.
other_cell_types: other cells in the LexA pattern (Fig. 4—fig. suppl. 1D)
penetrance: median about 4% of time antennal grooming (Fig. 4—fig. suppl. 1A)
notes: LexA line (aDN-LexA, R18C11 enhancer), not the GAL4. Front legs inferred from the Discussion.

title: A neural command circuit for grooming movement control.
quote: activation of aDN1 elicited about 50% fewer grooming bouts that terminated prior to the red light turning off
mapping_basis: synonyms.csv maps aDN1 to DNg62 only; line aDN1-spGAL4-1 listed as DNg62.
stimulation: 656-nm red light, 27 mW/cm2, 5 Hz (0.1 s on/off) for 5 s, 30 s interstimulus interval, 3 stimulations; in the dark
penetrance: Fig. 7D: fraction of flies grooming rises close to 1 at light onset, and bouts end before light off
notes: Antennal grooming is time-locked to the red light and does not persist after it. Front legs inferred from the Discussion.

title: A neural command circuit for grooming movement control.
